transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 09:30 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Turner (Redwood AE), Diego Mendez (Redwood SE), Sarah Li (Quantum CTO), Marcus Reed (Quantum SRE), Priya Sharma (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on p95 latency targets and throughput for both Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options. Customer needs streaming support and token/sec benchmarking for long-form responses (up to ~1k tokens) at 200 concurrent users, with p95 latency target ~800ms for short prompts and ~2.5s for 1k-token streaming. Discussed batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs and security requirements (SOC 2, VPC, KMS).

Topics: p95 targets; concurrency and burst; streaming behavior and token/sec; benchmarking plan; security docs; next steps and demo/POC scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: all right hi everyone thanks for joining this is ava from redwood, we got diego on the call as well, he is our se and will handle the throughput / perf details.
[00:12] Sarah: Hey thanks ava, i'm Sarah. quick context: Quantum Payments is building a realtime fraud scoring and conversational support assistant, so latency is huge for us. we want to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private, costs and p95 targets.
[00:25] Diego: great, thanks sarah. can you share your current baseline? like p95 today, average request size, and concurrency? even ballpark helps.
[00:34] Marcus: yeah currently we run an ensemble on our infra, p95 is around 1.8s for 256-token prompts, peak concurrency ~150, typical steady 40, but spikes to 250 during batch payouts. goal would be p95 <800ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and under 2.5s for 1k token streaming.
[00:56] Priya: and we do streaming for long responses so token/sec matters, we want consistent throughput not huge variance.
[01:08] Diego: okay got it. quick high-level — hosted is fastest to get started, simple API, good for lower throughput and non-sensitive data. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower p95s under load because you control capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance and data residency.
[01:30] Sarah: for compliance we'll need SOC2, SSO, audit logs and KMS integration — are those available for Dedicated?
[01:38] Ava: yes, Dedicated and Private both support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations. we'll send the security whitepaper after.
[01:46] Marcus: cool, thanks. about benchmarking — what config do you typically run for p95 token/sec tests? like model size, batch settings, quantization?
[01:56] Diego: good q. for benchmarking we usually run a profile with representative sequence lengths: short (32-128), medium (256-512), long (1k). we test on the model variants you plan to use — quantized weights vs fp16 — and measure both cold and warm KV cache. token/sec is measured during streaming steady-state; p95 is computed on end-to-end request latency including network.
[02:20] Sarah: do you have numbers for say a 1B-7B class model vs 13B on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:27] Diego: roughly, on Dedicated with A100-style instances a 7B model with quantization can hit ~60-80 tokens/sec steady with p95 for 256 calls under 300-400ms at 100 concurrent streams. 13B tends to be 20-40 tokens/sec depending on quant. Hosted will have similar per-node perf but multi-tenant noise means we size for p95 at higher buffers, so Dedicated usually gives 20-30% better p95 under heavy concurrency.
[02:55] Priya: that 60-80 tokens/sec, is that per GPU or per shard?
[03:01] Diego: that's per GPU in that config. with model sharding or tensor-parallel setups it's different. for streaming long outputs the per-GPU token/sec matters a lot because you want steady emission.
[03:12] Marcus: what about batching? we've got a lot of short prompts where batching could help, but we need low tail latency.
[03:20] Diego: batching is workload-dependent. continuous batching with adaptive time windows can increase throughput without hurting p95 too much if you cap max waiting ms before dispatch. we're able to tune batching policy — e.g., prefer latency SLOs for interactive routes and throughput SLOs for background routes.
[03:38] Sarah: interesting. do you support prefix/KV cache to speed up repeated contexts for the fraud model? we have long histories per user.
[03:45] Ava: yes we support prefix and KV caching; that often reduces tokens processed at inference time and improves p95 substantially for repeated contexts.
[03:52] Priya: about private deployment — we need an on-prem option for restricted datasets. how big a difference in p95 should we expect for on-prem vs Dedicated?
[04:01] Diego: on-prem mostly depends on your infra (networking, NVLink, GPU type). functionally it's the same runtime; if you give us A100 or Trn-like we can hit similar p95, but you'll need to tune kernel selection and quantization. Private also adds extra network latency if control plane is remote.
[04:18] Marcus: any caveats on streaming and load balancing? we noticed in our tests spikes cause head-of-line blocking.
[04:25] Diego: head-of-line is real for long streaming sequences. we mitigate with stream prioritization and lane-based routing — short requests get fast lanes. also preemption fallback where long-running streams can be preempted to keep p95 for interactive flows.
[04:41] Sarah: okay good. for the POC we want a bench: 200 concurrent streams, mix 60% short (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (256-512), 10% long (~1k tokens), target p95 800ms / 2.5s for long. can you run that on Dedicated and show token/sec and p95 curves?
[05:04] Diego: yes we can. i'll need sample prompt distributions and model choice (open model name or our curated variant). also want to test quantized vs fp16.
[05:14] Sarah: we'll provide sample prompts and a sample dataset. any limitations on streaming window or chunk sizes?
[05:20] Diego: we stream with chunk sizes tunable; by default 64-token chunks are common. token/sec measured at steady-state; if you stream tiny chunks you get higher overhead.
[05:29] Priya: pricing question: how do you price Dedicated if we need reserved capacity for sustained 200 conc?
[05:34] Ava: Dedicated is committed capacity + overage/bursting options. i'll send the pricing tiers and an example calc based on your concurrency and model selection.
[05:43] Marcus: for the benchmark — do you expose raw traces or pcap like traces so we can plot token emission over time?
[05:49] Diego: we provide per-token latency logs, per-request traces, and aggregate p95/p99 charts. we can also share raw CSVs for your analysis.
[05:58] Sarah: great. any security docs we need to evaluate for Private?
[06:03] Ava: we'll attach SOC2, our data processing addendum, and details on KMS + audit logs.
[06:10] Diego: oh and one more: if you need ultra-low cost, we can recommend quantization profiles and batching settings that lower cost at slight latency tradeoffs. we'll include those recommendations in the bench plan.
[06:23] Priya: do you have customers in payments? any references?
[06:26] Ava: yes, a few fintechs — i'll share anonymized reference notes and a short case study.
[06:32] Marcus: timeline — if we kick off next week how long is a basic Dedicated bench?
[06:36] Diego: typically 5 business days to run the full profile and assemble results if we have sample traffic and keys. faster if you accept default models.
[06:44] Sarah: perfect. ok let's recap.
[06:47] Ava: recap — action items: Ava will send pricing, security docs, and customer references; Diego will produce benchmarking plan and target configs and run Dedicated bench once sample prompts are provided; Sarah will share prompt dataset and concurrency profile. we'll target bench run next week and technical deep-dive on 2026-03-10. any other asks?
[07:08] Sarah: no that's it, thanks.
[07:11] Priya: thanks everyone.
[07:12] Ava: thanks all, talk soon.

Meeting end.
